title: The essential image of the comparison inverse image

source.place: Lemma 5.1.1 and the forward implication of Lemma 5.1.2 (p. 34); transport along an isomorphism written out

proof.text: $(2)\Rightarrow(3)$. By [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map], classicality says that for every affine ind-étale presentation $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ by affine étale $X$-schemes, the cocone $G(U_i)\to G(U)$ consisting of restriction maps exhibits $G(U)$ as the filtered colimit of the $G(U_i)$. This is precisely the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-continuous-counit-sets], with its sheaf $F$ specialized to $G$. That theorem applies to an arbitrary scheme $X$ and a sheaf of sets, and concludes that the comparison adjunction counit $\varepsilon_G:\nu_X^*\nu_{X,*}G\to G$ is invertible. Hence (3) holds. Here the colimit cocone is the specified restriction cocone, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target; this verifies the map required by the cited criterion.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.2, reverse implication, and the observation following Definition 5.1.3 (p. 34)

proof.text: $(3)\Rightarrow(1)$. The direct-image functor of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] sends $G$ to an étale sheaf of sets $F=\nu_{X,*}G$. The inverse of the counit isomorphism in (3) is an isomorphism $G\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_X^*F$, which supplies the witness in (1).
